# Best Conversational AI Platforms for Retail and Ecommerce Customer Service (2026)


## TL;DR


Retailers with substantial phone volume should compare SigmaMind AI and Retell AI for telephony fit, then test order access and human transfers. Ringly describes Shopify-focused phone workflows, including order lookups and escalation. For chat-led Shopify support, Gorgias centers order work in its helpdesk, while Fin for Ecommerce serves web Messenger. Start with the comparison table, then use the pilot checklist to test vendor-described capabilities with your own systems.


## Choose voice or chat first


Start with the channel that handles most of your support requests. Retailers with substantial phone volume need to check phone-system compatibility and transfers that preserve customer context. Stores led by chat or helpdesk tickets should prioritize order access and approved storefront actions.


Phone pilots should test after-hours routing, peak call volume, and whether a person receives the order details and conversation history during a transfer. Chat and helpdesk pilots should test which approved order and return actions an agent can complete within the tool.


An agent needs authorized access to current order data and your store's rules before it can take an approved return action. The pilot checklist below helps you confirm which capabilities work with your configuration.


## Comparison table: retail conversational AI platforms at a glance


Use the tables to shortlist providers by support channel, then demonstrate vendor-described capabilities before relying on them for order actions or phone support.


Channel Prioritize Check in a pilot


Voice Phone-system fit, after-hours coverage, and human transfers Order access, call handling under expected load, and context passed to a person


Chat or helpdesk Storefront access and approved order actions Which requests the agent can resolve within the tool


Provider Best for Key strength or documented fit Retail workflow and integration check Pricing


[SigmaMind AI](https://sigmamind.ai/) Retail contact centers with substantial phone volume Its[deployment documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) lists phone-system connections. Ask to see its omni-channel conversational flow builder and test voice latency under your expected load. Verify CRM access, order lookups, returns, and transfer context. A[partner-built Gorgias app](https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/sigmamind-ai-253905) documents Shopify-linked ticket workflows, not autonomous phone actions or a native Shopify app. Request a quote and confirm usage terms.


[Retell AI](https://docs.retellai.com/) Retailers able to configure voice agents and retail-system connections Its documentation describes voice agents, SIP connections, and warm transfers. Confirm order and return APIs, CRM fields, and transfer context. No native Shopify order action is established here.[Voice usage starts at $0.07/min](https://www.retellai.com/pricing) ; check component and concurrency costs.


[Ringly](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-that-actually-works-shopify) Shopify merchants needing after-hours phone coverage Ringly describes Shopify order lookups and return workflows by phone. Demonstrate approved actions, helpdesk handoffs, and fit with other contact-center systems. Confirm current plan and included minutes.


[Gorgias](https://www.gorgias.com/ecommerce/shopify) Shopify retailers managing orders in helpdesk tickets Its documented Shopify connection lets agents work with orders inside tickets. Confirm the AI Agent's scope; phone conversations do not establish autonomous AI call handling.[Helpdesk plans, AI resolutions, and voice usage](https://www.gorgias.com/pricing) have separate charges.


[Zowie](https://getzowie.com/blog/best-ai-customer-service-platforms-for-retail-2026) Retailers prepared to pilot automated workflows Zowie describes order and return Flows and claims voice support. Verify any Shopify connection, SIP support, completed actions, and human transfers. Request current pricing.


[Fin for Ecommerce](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/14997821-fin-for-ecommerce-explained) Shopify storefront support in web Messenger Intercom documents a Shopify connection for this ecommerce role. Verify the actions your store permits. This role does not support voice. Confirm current resolution pricing.


[Decagon](https://decagon.ai/) Enterprise buyers comparing custom retail connections Retail capabilities require published documentation or a demonstration. Request a demonstration of order actions, phone integration, and transfers. Request pricing.


A ticket integration does not establish autonomous phone support, and an API option does not establish a native Shopify connection.


## SigmaMind AI for retail contact centers with existing phone infrastructure


SigmaMind AI is best suited to retailers evaluating AI voice support for substantial call volume on existing contact-center infrastructure. Its[deployment documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) lists SIP, Twilio, VICIdial, and Five9 connections. Check the connection you use against your routing and deployment requirements. Ask SigmaMind AI to demonstrate its omni-channel conversational flow builder with your phone system and CRM. Under your expected call load, measure voice latency and call quality, then check what order and conversation context reaches a person during transfer.


For Shopify brands, SigmaMind AI describes a[partner integration with Wonderment](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/real-time-tracking-with-wonderment-sigmamind-ai-integration) for shipping and order-tracking information. Ask how SigmaMind AI receives Wonderment data and how recently it was updated before relying on delivery answers. The available documentation does not establish a native SigmaMind AI Shopify app. Returns execution would need access to your order system, return rules, and any required approval steps.


The[partner-built Gorgias app](https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/sigmamind-ai-253905) describes Shopify-linked ticket workflows for SigmaMind AI. That documentation does not establish which order or return requests a SigmaMind AI phone agent can resolve.


**Best for retailers with substantial call volume and existing telephony that want to add AI voice support.** A Shopify-first merchant primarily buying storefront chat and helpdesk automation should compare tools built around those workflows first.


## Retell AI for developer-built voice agents at retail call volume


Retell AI fits retailers that can build voice agents around their own order systems and phone setup. Retell AI’s[documentation](https://docs.retellai.com/) describes agent flows, IVR navigation, and warm transfers. Verify the available Salesforce and HubSpot connections and which contact or call fields they sync in your configuration. You can use Retell-managed numbers or connect existing telephony through SIP.


Retail order status and returns need separate validation. The reviewed Retell documentation does not document native Shopify actions for looking up orders, checking return eligibility, or issuing refunds. You would need to confirm how the agent connects to those systems. A pilot should also test whether a warm transfer gives the receiving agent the order number and conversation history, rather than assuming the transfer carries that context.


Retell lists[pay-as-you-go voice pricing](https://www.retellai.com/pricing) , with 20 concurrent calls included and a monthly charge for additional concurrency. Selected voice components, telephony, and add-ons affect the total bill.


**Best for retailers with engineering resources** to configure phone routing and connect retail workflows. Retell offers configurable voice agents, but the cited documentation does not establish an out-of-the-box Shopify returns agent.


## Ringly for Shopify-first phone support


Ringly markets 24/7 inbound phone coverage to Shopify merchants handling order and return inquiries. In its[Shopify voice AI overview](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-that-actually-works-shopify) , Ringly says its agent looks up live Shopify orders, supports return and exchange workflows, and shares transcript and order context with a helpdesk when it escalates a caller to a person. Check which return actions the agent can complete under your store’s policy.


Test Ringly's Shopify workflows with recently changed orders and check when those changes appear in its answers. During an escalation, inspect the context the human agent actually receives.


Ringly is best for Shopify-centric merchants whose main support gap is phone coverage. If you rely on several order systems or an established contact-center CRM, ask Ringly to demonstrate those connections and the human handoff before choosing it.


## Storefront and helpdesk options: Gorgias, Fin for Ecommerce, and Zowie


Gorgias fits retailers that manage support through Shopify-linked tickets. Its[Shopify helpdesk documentation](https://www.gorgias.com/ecommerce/shopify) says agents can see order history and create, edit, and refund orders inside tickets. Gorgias offers phone support within its helpdesk, but the cited Shopify documentation does not establish autonomous AI handling of high-volume inbound calls. When estimating cost, account for[ticket-based Helpdesk plans, AI Agent resolution charges, and voice usage](https://www.gorgias.com/pricing) separately. **Best for Shopify-first retailers that want agents to handle order work inside a multichannel helpdesk.**


Fin for Ecommerce fits Shopify support in web Messenger, not retail phone queues. Intercom[documents a native Shopify connection](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/14997821-fin-for-ecommerce-explained) for catalog and order data, including support for cart changes and post-purchase requests. Intercom says this ecommerce role does not support voice, even though other Fin offerings include voice. **Best for Shopify merchants that want AI assistance with shopping and support in web Messenger.**


Zowie presents a possible option for retailers evaluating automated workflows across channels, but its retail integration depth needs confirmation. In its[own retail comparison](https://getzowie.com/blog/best-ai-customer-service-platforms-for-retail-2026) , Zowie says its Flows can handle order tracking and returns, and it claims voice support with SIP compatibility. The available source does not verify a native Shopify connector, show how phone calls transfer to agents, or establish what requires API or middleware work. **Best for retailers willing to evaluate Zowie's claimed workflows in a pilot before relying on them for Shopify actions or phone coverage.**


## Decagon for a broader enterprise evaluation


Decagon remains an enterprise evaluation option here because this article does not cite published evidence for specific retail integrations or phone workflows. Ask Decagon for product documentation and a demonstration of order actions, phone integration, context-preserving transfers, and pricing against your requirements.


**Best for enterprise buyers prepared to validate retail connections and phone workflows directly.** If you are comparing platforms across industries, see the[broader customer-service guide](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/best-conversational-ai-platforms-customer-service) .


## How to pilot retail workflows


Use the same sample orders and return rules for each vendor pilot. For phone products, keep the queues and escalation scenarios consistent. Ask each vendor to identify actions supported by a native integration and those requiring an API or middleware.


- Test order-status answers against records the agent is authorized to access. Include a delayed shipment and a recently changed order, then check the data's freshness and whether the answer matches the current record.
- Test whether the agent executes your returns policy or only describes it. Try an expired return window and an ineligible item, then inspect your returns system for any actions the agent took.
- Route after-hours calls through your existing phone system. At expected peak load, check call handling and failed lookups, and confirm how callers reach a person when needed.
- Request a person midway through a call. Check whether the receiving agent gets the order number, reason for contact, and conversation transcript without asking the caller to start over. Inspect where those details appear in your CRM or helpdesk.
- If you support multiple store locations, test promotion-driven overflow, store-hours questions, and routing to the right location. Ask product-availability questions only if the vendor has verified authorized access to location-specific inventory and a way to check freshness. When the data cannot be trusted, the agent should direct the caller to a person.


## Call-quality monitoring and conversation accuracy scoring


Score conversation accuracy separately from completed actions. Review call recordings for request understanding, use of authorized and current order data, compliance with the return policy, and context passed during transfer. Compare each reported action with the order or return record. If a vendor supplies automated QA scores, compare a sample with human review before relying on them.


## FAQs


- **Can these platforms handle order status and returns automatically?**[Ringly says](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-that-actually-works-shopify) its phone agent looks up Shopify orders and handles return and exchange workflows. Gorgias says helpdesk agents can[view and change Shopify orders](https://www.gorgias.com/ecommerce/shopify) inside tickets. That does not establish that its AI Agent completes those actions autonomously. For SigmaMind AI or Retell AI, ask each vendor to demonstrate order-data access and any return actions against your policy. Do not assume either offers a ready-made Shopify refund workflow.
- **Can AI cover calls 24/7 and during seasonal surges?**[Ringly describes](https://www.ringly.io/blog/voice-ai-that-actually-works-shopify) 24/7 inbound phone coverage. For any phone vendor, test your expected peak call volume, including transfers to people when the queue is busy. Around-the-clock availability alone does not establish surge capacity.
- **Will it work with our phone system and CRM?**[Retell AI documents](https://docs.retellai.com/) bring-your-own telephony and several CRM connections.[SigmaMind AI’s deployment documentation](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/) lists phone-system connections. Ask for a demonstration with your phone platform, CRM records, and routing rules because a listed connection does not establish that it covers your configuration.
- **Does it integrate natively with Shopify?** Gorgias documents a Shopify helpdesk connection, and Ringly describes Shopify order lookups. Check the current integration and data-access scope for the product you plan to use. A[partner-built Gorgias integration](https://docs.gorgias.com/en-US/sigmamind-ai-253905) connects SigmaMind AI to Shopify-linked ticket workflows, but it does not establish a first-party SigmaMind AI Shopify app.
- **How does a human handoff preserve context?** Ringly says its escalation shares the transcript and order context. Retell AI documents warm transfers, but you should verify whether your agent receives the transcript, order number, and reason for transfer in the queue you use.


## Conclusion


If calls dominate your support volume, compare SigmaMind AI and Retell AI against your existing telephony, and include Ringly for Shopify-focused phone workflows. If chat and tickets dominate, compare Gorgias, Fin for Ecommerce, and Zowie against the order and return actions your agents need.


Before committing, test order-data accuracy, approved return actions, and the information a human agent receives during transfer using your own retail systems.
